title: IAF Jets Paint Tricolour Over Somnath's Sacred Skies
excerpt: India's Suryakiran aerobatic team roars over the ancient Jyotirlinga in a first-ever flypast marking 75 years of the temple's reconstruction.
body:
On May 11, 2026, six Indian Air Force jets streaked over one of Hinduism's holiest sites — and the skies above Somnath Temple have never looked quite like this before.

**What happened — jets, smoke and sacred ritual:**
The IAF's Suryakiran Aerobatic Team (SKAT) performed a 15-minute precision display above the Somnath Temple complex in Gujarat, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi watching from the ground. Six Hawk Mk-132 aircraft executed close-formation manoeuvres at speeds between 800 and 900 kilometres per hour. A standout moment: the jets released saffron, white and green smoke trails using indigenous pods built at the IAF's Base Repair Depot in Nashik, painting the Tricolour across the Arabian Sea sky. An IAF Chetak helicopter simultaneously showered flower petals over the temple as devotees chanted prayers below.

**Why this moment matters — bhakti, shakti and 75 years:**
The event marks the Somnath Amrut Mahotsav — 75 years since the reconstructed temple was inaugurated by President Dr Rajendra Prasad in 1951, after centuries of repeated destruction and revival. Modi, who chairs the Shree Somnath Trust, participated in Kumbhabhishek, Dhwaj Puja and Maha Puja rituals before the aerial display began. He later released a commemorative stamp and coin. On social media, Modi wrote that 'this spirit of Bhakti and Shakti filled every heart with deep joy.' The display was also the first-ever aerobatic show over the Somnath Temple, with Flight Lieutenant Kanwal Sandhu noting the historic nature of the moment. SKAT, founded in 1996, has now completed over 800 air displays globally.

**What to watch — a civilisational statement:**
India's government has signalled that the Somnath commemorations are part of a broader cultural and civilisational assertion — watch for further events under the Somnath Swabhiman Parv series connecting this milestone to the 1,000-year history of the shrine.
